message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade counter-offer in Monopoly.

The counter-offer is $100 for Mediterranean Avenue. I have $880 and own three properties. p2 has $911 and owns several railroads. p1 has $98 but holds a dangerous orange monopoly with three houses each.

p1 also owns Vermont, mortgaged St. Charles, States, and Water Works. p4 has a get-out-of-jail-free card and $366 in jail. Mediterranean is worth $60 with a $30 mortgage value. Completing browns would help p2 but brown properties are weak.

$100 cash beats the $30 mortgage value. Mediterranean is dead equity because p2 already owns Baltic. I am calculating orange rent values to assess survival risk.

Standard orange rent values are $450, $550, and $600. With $880 cash, surviving a New York Avenue hit would leave $280, and a Tennessee Avenue hit would leave $330.

Taking $100 would raise cash to $980, giving a $380 cushion against a New York Avenue hit. I am weighing whether to counter at $125 instead. A completed brown monopoly would only yield low rent even with hotels, so it is unlikely to bankrupt p1 directly. The real danger remains p1's orange monopoly.

Selling Mediterranean to p2 could actually help me. A completed brown monopoly might tax p1, and p2 would spend cash building browns rather than threatening me with yellows. The $100 offer is fair for a $60 property, but splitting at $125 is reasonable. I will not sell Boardwalk and I will not feed p1.

Accepting $100 is the "lower once" option. Countering to $125 risks p2 rejecting and leaving me stuck with dead equity. The $100 offer is locked in if accepted. I will accept the current offer.

I will counter at $125. This is a reasonable compromise that still discounts the original $150 offer. I am unsure if rejecting a counter ends the trade or allows another exchange.

I will accept the $100 offer. The certainty of that cash is more valuable than risking a rejection for a $25 difference. I also notice p4 owns Park Place and I own Boardwalk, creating a dark blue split.
